\section[derrochar]{derrochar — to waste, to squander}

\label{lesson:ES-C627-derrochar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for guilty, then the Spanish for the fraud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: derrochar}
\textbf{derrochar} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste, to squander\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No derroches el dinero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do not waste your money.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El derroche} — the waste.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{derrochar} is not settled; one account links it to French \emph{dérocher} 'to throw down from a rock', and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derrochar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{derrochar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{derrochar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for guilty, then the Spanish for the fraud, then say \emph{derrochar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does derrochar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To waste, to squander\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el ingreso]{el ingreso — the income; the deposit; admission}

\label{lesson:ES-C627-ingreso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the fraud, then the Spanish for to waste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el ingreso}
\textbf{el ingreso} — \textquotedblleft{}the income; the deposit; admission\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mis ingresos son bajos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My income is low.}
\end{quote}

In the plural it is income. \emph{El ingreso en el hospital} — hospital admission.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ingreso} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ingressus} 'an entering', built on \emph{ingredi} 'to step in', from \emph{gradi} 'to step' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el ingreso}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el ingreso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el ingreso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the fraud, then the Spanish for to waste, then say \emph{el ingreso} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el ingreso mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The income; the deposit; admission\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la deuda]{la deuda — the debt}

\label{lesson:ES-C627-deuda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to waste, then the Spanish for the income.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la deuda}
\textbf{la deuda} — \textquotedblleft{}the debt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tengo una deuda con el banco.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have a debt with the bank.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar en deuda con} — to be in debt to, also in a moral sense.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{deuda} is inherited from Latin \emph{debita} 'things owed', through Old Spanish \emph{debda}, from \emph{debere} 'to owe' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la deuda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la deuda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la deuda}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to waste, then the Spanish for the income, then say \emph{la deuda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la deuda mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The debt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[endeudarse]{endeudarse — to get into debt}

\label{lesson:ES-C627-endeudarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the income, then the Spanish for the debt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: endeudarse}
\textbf{endeudarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to get into debt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se endeudó para comprar un coche.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He got into debt to buy a car.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{la deuda}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{endeudarse} is built on \emph{deuda} 'debt', inherited from Latin \emph{debita} 'things owed', from \emph{debere} 'to owe' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[invertir]{invertir — to invest; to reverse}

\label{lesson:ES-C627-invertir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the debt, then the Spanish for to get into debt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: invertir}
\textbf{invertir} — \textquotedblleft{}to invest; to reverse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Quiero invertir en mi educación.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I want to invest in my education.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{sentir}: \emph{invierto, invirtió}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{invertir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{invertere} 'to turn upside down', built from \emph{in} and \emph{vertere} 'to turn' (EtymDB); the money sense came later.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{invertir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{invertir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{invertir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the debt, then the Spanish for to get into debt, then say \emph{invertir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
